Input and focus.question: What happens when switching to another application during an unfinished brush stroke or object drag?
Input and focus.answer: Cancel the unfinished gesture and restore the state before that stroke or drag.
options_presented: Commit it up to that point
Input and focus.notes: User selected 1 and selected all four Phase 5 discussion areas. Already committed work remains durable; do not create an undo step for cancelled previews.

Input and focus.question: What happens if the pointer moves over a side panel while the mouse button or pen remains down?
Input and focus.answer: Keep the gesture active until release; prevent panel controls from activating and keep brush painting within the canvas.
options_presented: Keep the gesture active until release (recommended)
Finish the gesture at the canvas edge
Input and focus.notes: User selected 1. Retain pointer capture across canvas/panel boundaries; release ends the gesture. Application focus loss still cancels under the prior decision. Tablet-as-pointer scope remains; pressure is deferred.

Input and focus.question: How should numeric fields such as size, rotation and opacity apply changes?
Input and focus.answer: Preview live; Enter or leaving the field commits one undo step, Escape restores the previous value.
Input and focus.notes: User selected 1. Document-property edits form one durable undo step per completed edit, not one per keystroke. Tool-default settings remain tool state rather than fabricating document history. In-app field-focus change commits; handling numeric drafts during application deactivation is a design detail that must not conflict with cancellation of active canvas gestures.

Input and focus.question: How should keyboard tool switching work?
Input and focus.answer: Single-key shortcuts when the canvas has focus, shown in tooltips; text and numeric typing take precedence.
options_presented: Single-key shortcuts when canvas has focus (recommended)
Input and focus.notes: User selected 1. Exact tool bindings remain design proposals. Ordinary text/numeric editing, dialogs and focused lists must not be intercepted by canvas tool shortcuts.
